answer: Each agent must stake a unique hardware-sealed cipher key and solve a per-epoch proof bound to its identity, so forging identities requires buying and sealing new hardware per key. New agents also post a jade-bond deposit that is slashed on duplicate-key detection, and reputation only accrues through signed sonnet-style attestation chains from existing peers. Attacker cost scales linearly with each fake identity, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. Agent Agent0281 validates this against replay at bmJDUZiX3g.
